body.objective: Students will be able to use prepositions with places.
body.iCan: I can use prepositions with places.
successCriteria: I can use à, en, au and aux correctly with places
I can talk about where I am going and where I have been
I can plan a trip itinerary in French
body.hook: You're planning a trip: Paris, then Brussels, then Dakar, then back home to Canada. In French, you'd say "à Paris," "en Belgique," "au Sénégal" and "au Canada": four different words for "to" or "in." It looks random, but the rule is simple once you know it.

vocabulary.definition: Used with cities (à Paris, à Montréal).
Used with feminine countries and those starting with a vowel (en France, en Italie, en Iran).
Used with masculine countries (au Canada, au Japon, au Sénégal).
Used with plural countries (aux États-Unis, aux Pays-Bas).

study.title: Mon itinéraire
study.question: How do I talk about where I'm going in French?
study.passage:
The rule:
• Cities: à → à Paris, à Calgary, à Tokyo
• Feminine countries (most end in -e): en → en France, en Belgique, en Suisse, en Chine, en Espagne
• Countries starting with a vowel: en → en Iran, en Israël, en Afghanistan
• Masculine countries: au → au Canada, au Mexique, au Japon, au Maroc, au Sénégal (le Mexique ends in -e but is masculine!)
• Plural countries: aux → aux États-Unis, aux Pays-Bas
• Provinces: au Québec, au Manitoba, en Alberta, en Ontario, en Colombie-Britannique
Dialogue:
Zoé : Cet été, je vais faire un grand voyage !
Félix : Ah oui ? Où vas-tu ?
Zoé : D'abord, je vais à Paris, en France. Ensuite, je vais en Belgique pour visiter Bruxelles. Puis je vais au Sénégal, à Dakar, pour voir ma tante.
Félix : Super ! Comment vas-tu voyager ?
Zoé : En avion, sauf entre Paris et Bruxelles : je vais prendre le train.
Félix : Moi, je reste au Canada. Je vais au Québec avec ma famille.
English support: Cet été = this summer; sauf = except; je reste = I'm staying.
Activity: Plan a 10-day trip to three francophone places (at least one city, one feminine country and one masculine country). Write your itinerary and present it.
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.
steps: Learn à, en, au and aux
Sort countries and provinces by preposition
Read the dialogue with a partner
discussion: Why is it "au Mexique" even though Mexique ends in -e?
Which countries does Zoé visit, and with which prepositions?
How does Zoé travel between Paris and Brussels?
study.product: Write a 10-day itinerary (8–10 sentences) for a trip to three francophone destinations, using à, en, au or aux correctly for each and saying how you will travel.

examples.title: Plural and provinces
examples.problem: Say "They're going to the United States and to Alberta."
examples.answer: Ils vont aux États-Unis et en Alberta.

practice.q: Which preposition goes with feminine countries?
Which preposition goes with masculine countries?
Which preposition goes with plural countries?
How does Zoé travel from Paris to Brussels?
Why is it "en Iran" although Iran is masculine?
practice.a: Countries starting with a vowel use en.
It ends in -e but is masculine, so it takes au.

practice.q: Say "I'm going to Dakar, in Senegal."
practice.a: Je vais à Dakar, au Sénégal.

practice.q: Write a sentence with three destinations.
practice.a: Sample: Je vais à Paris, en Belgique et au Maroc.

misconceptions: Assuming every country ending in -e is feminine
exitTicket: Choose the correct preposition for a city, a feminine country and a masculine country.
Say where you'd like to travel.

test.title: Practice test: Use prepositions with places

items.q: State the rule for à, en, au and aux.
items.answer: À cities; en feminine or vowel countries; au masculine; aux plural.

items.q: How do you say "I'm going to Japan"?

items.answer: It ends in -e but is masculine, so it takes au.
Paris in France, Brussels in Belgium, then Dakar in Senegal, by plane and train.

items.q: Write a sentence about where you live.
items.answer: Sample: J'habite à Red Deer, en Alberta, au Canada.

items.q: Explain why prepositions matter for clear communication.
items.answer: They show the type of place and are expected in correct French.
